case: L1 Workshop — Dominique, the 3 core functions of a business (Frame.io REVIEW pair, not a published reel)
_note: This is a REVIEW-derived calibration pair: we shipped V3, Oliver (the team's editor) left Frame.io notes, and OLIVER_review_cut is the cut his notes produce. Unlike cases 001-007 (his published reels), the 'answer key' here is his REVISION of our cut — so it directly shows the tightness gap between our cut and his taste. Source: ~/Downloads/alex/2026-06-17_StageQA dom_v3 (29.97fps, 107.4s).
RAW_full_interaction: we've essentially made $20 million in revenue across all our different companies. what I was essentially asking, for any business other than a CEO and the founder, what would be the three core members or roles that any business would need in order to succeed? so the first thing I'll do is I'll just kind of challenge the question, which is that it's not like, what are the three key people? so I could just be like, I'll reject the premise. it's more so, what are the functions? what things must occur in a business and whether one person does them or 20 people do them, these things have to happen. at the most foundational level, you have to have someone who can promote, someone who can advertise, let people know about the stuff. now that also technically includes conversion. so that one person who goes and gets customers. the other person is the person who builds the thing. who's the one who's at head of product or the service, making sure that it continues to be exceptional. and then the third kind of function is who's running the day-to-day, who's operating, who's leading the team? who's continuing to basically build the culture? who's the one who's recruiting the people in, setting the standards for how the company runs? now, there's the things that have to occur. one person can do all three of those things. if you're asking the question of who do we need to hire for each of our portfolio companies, I would just say, where is the deficiency with each of those companies? and does that deficiency tie to the constraint of the business? so if you're demand constrained and no one in the company knows how to advertise, that makes sense. if you're not demand constrained and no one knows how to advertise, who cares? it's not the constraint today. so we still always start with, are we supply or demand constrained? and once we know which one we are, because you really can, for the most part, just be one of the two, we basically ignore everything else on the other side.
OUR_shipped_cut: (= RAW above, essentially uncut — that was the defect; too loose, kept all the slack/filler/elaboration and ran to a wind-down ending.)
OLIVER_review_cut: we've essentially made $20 million in revenue across all our different companies. for any business other than a CEO and the founder, what would be the three core roles that any business would need in order to succeed? so the first thing I'll do is I'll just kind of challenge the question. it's not like, what are the three key people? it's more so, what are the functions? what things must occur in a business, and whether one person does them or 20 people do them, these things have to happen. at the most foundational level, you have to have someone who can promote, someone who can advertise, let people know about the stuff. the other person is the one who builds the thing, who's at head of product or the service, making sure it continues to be exceptional. and then the third kind of function is who's running the day-to-day, who's operating, who's leading the team, who's building the culture, who's recruiting the people and setting the standards for how the company runs. one person can do all three of those things. if you're asking who to hire for each of your portfolio companies, I would just say: where is the deficiency, and does that deficiency tie to the constraint of the business? so if you're demand constrained and no one knows how to advertise, that makes sense. if you're NOT demand constrained and no one knows how to advertise, who cares? it's not the constraint today.

the ~1.8s dead hesitation inside 'CEO and the —— founder' (keep the words)
meta-aside 'so I could just be like, I'll reject the premise.'
same-point elaboration 'now that also technically includes conversion. so that one person who goes and gets customers.'
the harsh-splice gap before 'if you're asking' (re-cut seam clean)

calibration_2026_06_22.method: Oliver left 23 Frame.io notes on our V3; bucketed + mapped to the transcript. The pattern (not a single miss): our cut was TOO LOOSE.
calibration_2026_06_22.dominant_lesson: TIGHTNESS — ~half the notes. Our Q&A cut keeps slack Oliver removes: (1) inter-sentence DEAD AIR (after 'succeed?', 'happen.', 'business?', held words), (2) CONNECTIVE-TISSUE filler mid-clip ('which is that', 'so I could just be like', 'what I was essentially asking'), (3) SAME-POINT elaboration that restates a mechanism ('now that also technically includes conversion…'), (4) a WIND-DOWN ending instead of the punchline.
calibration_2026_06_22.ending_lesson: END ON THE PUNCHLINE: Oliver cut 10.7s of recap/wind-down to land on 'it's not the constraint today.' Our boundary over-ran past the payoff into 'so we still always start with… we basically ignore everything else.' (Confirms the qa_editorial WINDDOWN gate — but it shipped anyway, so the boundary-picker isn't ending tight.)
calibration_2026_06_22.caption_lessons: numerals not spelled-out (three->3, third->3rd: baked in spice_normalize); 2 Whisper mishearings survived ('other than a'->'the', 'there's the things'->'those are the things': audit-captions force-align must run pre-delivery); one emphasis-quote phrase (#FED90F + italic + quotes: now a registered caption color).
calibration_2026_06_22.other_bakes: NO music on Q&A (baked); harsh-seam gate in reqc (click=FAIL, abrupt-onset=advisory); G8 PACING gate in qa_prebuild_audit flags loose dead-air + leftover connective filler pre-encode.
rejected_overfit_rules: 'Auto-strip all mid-clip discourse markers in the build' — REJECTED: 'so'/'now'/'well' are frequently load-bearing mid-sentence; a blanket strip mangles meaning. Target connective TISSUE in the clipper, not a mechanical global strip.

'Auto-trim every dead-air pause in qa_assembly' — REJECTED: auto-trimming pauses on the single-cam Alex-answer re-opens the documented JUMP-CUT regression (61 shipped once) + clipped words. Use a pre-encode GATE that flags loose pauses for the editor, with the reqc jump-cut gate as backstop — don't auto-mutate from n=1.
calibration_2026_06_22.net: n=1 review. The patterns (tightness, end-on-punchline) CONFIRM existing rules rather than reveal new ones — the gap is ENFORCEMENT/application, not missing rules. Action: this case is the regression test; clipper prompt sharpened on connective-tissue + same-point elaboration; G8 gate surfaces loose pacing pre-encode. HARDEN the mechanical dead-air default only after this pattern recurs across ≥3 reviews (per the compounding cadence).
